content.title: About
content.content: The Greyhound is a dog breed renowned for its exceptional speed and elegance. Originally bred in England for hare hunting, it has become a symbol of lightness and grace. Greyhounds feature a sleek, aerodynamic body, long legs, and a deep chest, allowing them to reach speeds of up to 70 km/h.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greyhounds can accelerate to 70 km/h, making them among the fastest land animals.
These dogs have a unique ability to “freeze” in place when stopped, thanks to powerful hind muscles.
Greyhounds often compete in dog racing, where their speed is measured over short distances.
Unlike many breeds, Greyhounds shed very little and require minimal coat maintenance.
They are known for their calm home demeanor and are sometimes called “pencils” because of their thin, elongated shape.

items.title: Improved Owner Physical Activity
items.content: Greyhound owners frequently engage in running or active walks, which benefits cardiovascular health and overall fitness.

items.title: Stress Reduction
items.content: Having a calm, affectionate companion helps lower cortisol levels and improves emotional well‑being.

items.title: Development of Responsibility
items.content: Caring for a breed that requires regular exercise fosters discipline and a sense of responsibility in the owner.

items.title: Cold Sensitivity
items.content: Their thin coat and low body fat make Greyhounds vulnerable to low temperatures; a warm jacket is recommended in cold weather.

items.title: Exercise Requirements
items.content: Insufficient daily runs can lead to behavioral issues and weight gain.

items.title: Joint Injury Susceptibility
items.content: Because of their long legs and high speed, Greyhounds are prone to strains and sprains, especially during sudden starts.

content.title: How to Care
content.content: Greyhounds need daily walks, preferably with running sessions. Their short coat should be brushed weekly to remove loose hair. Regularly check paws and trim nails as needed. In cold weather, use a warm sweater or coat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: If you cannot provide constant outdoor exercise, keep the Greyhound in a spacious indoor area with a soft floor where it can move freely. Ensure access to fresh water and a comfortable temperature.
